title.description:
A short description of the example; useful if there are multiple examples. This may contain simple inline
markup such as would appear within a paragraph, but no block markup.

When examples are parsed from a documentation comment, the title is taken from the first line of content,
if it's not a fenced code block. This can appear on the same line as the annotation or on the subsequent line,
but before any code.

lang.description:
Language of the example code. This is not necessarily a programming language, but is more a high-level label
for the specific example.

group.description:
If this example is part of a group with the same code in different languages, this field will be the same
for all the examples in the group.

When examples are parsed from a documentation comment, the group is auto-assigned a unique number so each
`@example` annotation is a separate group. Note that multiple code blocks, each for a different language, may
appear within a single annotation and they all will share a title.

synthesized.description:
Whether this was synthesized by the system as a generic example.

@see #synthesize

title:
Example code extracted from, or generated for, a piece of documented structure.

Note that the `@example` annotation will collect content until the next annotation or the end of the comment.
Within it only fenced code blocks, with {@link DocumentationExample.Language valid languages} specified,
are allowed.

A title can optionally be provided immediately after the annotation and before any fenced code blocks (either on the
same line as the annotation or the next line).

@example Declaring examples
```type
/**
 * @return the sum of all arguments
 *
 * @example Summing values
 * ```js
 * let sum = Arithmetic.sum(2, 3, 4);
 * ```
 * ```py
 * sum = c3.Arithmetic.sum(2, 3, 4)
 * ```
```
name: DocumentationExample
